channel.title: Jerrin Mathew: Writing
channel.description: Psychiatric care for Chicago and Illinois professionals.

item.title: After the ICU: What Families Go Through, and Why It Has a Name
item.description: Anxiety, depression, and trauma symptoms in family members after a loved one's ICU stay are common enough to have a name, PICS-F. What it looks like, who is at risk, and what helps, from an ICU nurse.

item.title: Seasonal Depression in Chicago: Why Winter Hits Harder Here
item.description: Why Chicago winters bring on seasonal depression, how to tell the winter blues from seasonal affective disorder, and which treatments have evidence.

item.title: Free and Low-Cost Mental Health Care in Chicago
item.description: Where to find free and low-cost mental health care in Chicago: the city's mental health centers, library counseling, helplines, and other affordable options.

item.title: How to Find a Psychiatrist in Chicago, and What to Do While You Wait
item.description: How to find a psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner in Chicago: where to look, what to ask when you call, and how to get support while you wait.

item.title: Your Mental Health Insurance Rights in Illinois
item.description: What Illinois parity law requires of health insurers, which plans it covers, and how to appeal when a mental health or substance use claim is denied.

item.title: Sports Betting in Illinois: When It Stops Being Fun
item.description: How legal sports betting in Illinois has changed gambling, the signs that betting has become a problem, and where to get free help in Illinois.

item.title: Autism and ADHD Together
item.description: Autism and ADHD co-occur far more often than once believed. How the two interact, why one often masks the other, and why it matters for treatment.

item.title: Autism Diagnosed in Adulthood: Why Capable People Get Missed
item.description: Why autism is frequently missed until adulthood in intelligent, high-functioning people, and what an adult assessment looks for.

item.title: Autistic Burnout Is Not Ordinary Burnout
item.description: Autistic burnout involves loss of skills and capacity, not just exhaustion. How it differs from occupational burnout and depression, and what recovery needs.

item.title: Masking: The Cost of Performing Normal at Work
item.description: Masking is the effortful suppression of autistic traits to fit in. Why it is exhausting, what it costs over years, and how it shows up in professionals.

item.title: Exposure and Response Prevention: What OCD Treatment Actually Involves
item.description: ERP is the first-line psychological treatment for OCD. What it involves session by session, why it works, and why general talk therapy usually does not.

item.title: Intrusive Thoughts: What They Mean and What They Do Not
item.description: Nearly everyone has intrusive thoughts. Why they become sticky in OCD, why they do not reveal hidden desires, and why reassurance makes them worse.

item.title: OCD in High-Stakes Professions
item.description: How OCD shows up in physicians, nurses, attorneys, and pilots, why checking can look like diligence, and when conscientiousness becomes a disorder.

item.title: OCD Is Not About Being Tidy
item.description: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is widely misunderstood as neatness. What it actually involves, the forms it takes, and why it is so often missed.

item.title: EMDR, DBT, ACT: What the Acronyms Actually Mean
item.description: A plain explanation of the therapy acronyms you will encounter, what each treats, and which ones have the strongest evidence.

item.title: "Just Talk to Someone" Is Useless Advice
item.description: Therapy is not one thing. A guide to the main evidence-based approaches, what each is actually for, and how to choose rather than guess.

item.title: Therapy for People Who Analyze Everything
item.description: Insight is not change. Why highly analytical professionals often stall in therapy, and what actually moves things.

item.title: What Actually Happens in CBT
item.description: A session-by-session account of what cognitive behavioral therapy involves, what the homework is for, and why it feels like a course rather than a conversation.

item.title: Why a Prescriber Should Understand Psychotherapy
item.description: Why psychiatric prescribers who understand psychotherapy make better medication decisions, and what gets missed when they do not.

item.title: The Antidepressant Side Effects People Do Not Bring Up
item.description: Sexual side effects, emotional blunting, and weight change are common on antidepressants and frequently go unmentioned. Why raising them matters.

item.title: Coming Off Psychiatric Medication Safely
item.description: How to stop a psychiatric medication properly: why tapering matters, what discontinuation symptoms feel like, and how to tell them apart from relapse.

item.title: Starting an Antidepressant: What the First Eight Weeks Actually Feel Like
item.description: A realistic timeline for starting an antidepressant: what happens in week one, when improvement typically begins, and which side effects fade.

item.title: Stimulant Medication for Adult ADHD: What It Does and Does Not Do
item.description: What stimulant medication for adult ADHD actually changes, what it will not fix, and how prescribing works in practice.

item.title: Therapy, Medication, or Both?
item.description: How to think about the choice between psychotherapy and medication, when combining them helps most, and what the evidence actually supports.

item.title: Why Your Medication Stopped Working
item.description: A psychiatric medication that helped for years can stop working. The possible reasons, what to check first, and what actually helps.

item.title: Diagnostic Formulation in Psychiatry: What It Is, With an Example
item.description: What a diagnostic formulation in psychiatry is, the four P's model, and a worked example showing how a formulation shapes treatment beyond the diagnosis.

item.title: ADHD at Work: How Professionals Cope When They Aren’t Getting Treatment
item.description: How adults with untreated ADHD compensate at work, why the compensation is invisible, and when coping is no longer enough.

item.title: ADHD in Attorneys: When the Work Demands More Executive Function Than It Appears
item.description: Why ADHD is often missed in attorneys who shine in court but drown in deadlines and paperwork, and what a proper adult ADHD assessment involves.

item.title: ADHD in CEOs: When Intelligence Isn’t the Problem
item.description: ADHD in senior executives is often masked by intelligence, delegation, and elaborate systems. Why success does not rule out the diagnosis.

item.title: ADHD in Chicago Physicians and Surgeons: Recognition and Evidence-Based Treatment
item.description: How ADHD presents in physicians and surgeons in Chicago. Recognition, barriers to care, and evidence-based treatment options for medical professionals.
